sections.title: Architecture
sections.content: Evidence-gated artifact DAG separates lifecycle authority from Bootstrap execution. Acceptance owns closure, deterministic checks, route, imports, and finalization; Bootstrap emits non-authorizing evidence only. Immutable identity-bound artifacts, complete closures, isolated segments, required-check receipts, event recovery, typed routes, and rollout parity are required.

sections.title: Contract
sections.content: Acceptance begins only from a current identity-bound implementation-complete handoff, freezes baseline and candidate, computes complete Consumer Closure, runs contract-projected checks, selects supervised or unattended mode plus typed route, and finalizes only exact-matched current evidence. Candidate or authority changes stale dependent evidence.

sections.title: Lifecycle
sections.content: VDD owns draft and plan-ready; maintainer owns implementation-authorized and supervised non-authorizing decisions; Quick Dev owns implementation-complete; Acceptance alone owns acceptance-passed. Deterministic-only routes avoid Bootstrap only under the fixed mode-route matrix; registered risks require full conformance or manual pause.

sections.title: Review Inputs
sections.content: Selected authority is delivered whole within budget, with exact continuation of partial reads. Over-budget inputs require controller-owned source-hash-bound range projections. Each child uses an immutable descriptor, frozen segment-only snapshot, absolute path, and inherited access proof; unassigned or mutated scope fails.

sections.title: Execution Recovery
sections.content: Append-only Process Events distinguish liveness from validated Effective Progress. Heartbeats, stdout, and polling do not refresh no-progress. Policy-bound watchdog, terminal reconciliation, leases, and bounded segment-local retry produce typed non-authorizing recovery outcomes when evidence is incomplete.

sections.title: Review Semantics
sections.content: Complete Bootstrap review retains isolated Blind Hunter, Edge Case Hunter, and Acceptance Auditor roles. Required checks precede semantic work; deterministic failure launches zero reviewers. Independent verification applies only to gate-accepted P0/P1 findings under existing risk/model policy.

sections.title: Verification
sections.content: M0 establishes isolation and recovery controls, M1 adds Acceptance strategy, and M2 validates 8-13-scale regression, semantic corpus, cost telemetry, and final import. Optimization cannot omit authority, weaken routes, convert transport failures into semantics, or create false authorization.
